template.name: The Workhouse and the Weight of Systems

assignments.text:
What was Oliver’s horror and alarm as he stood a few paces off, looking on with
his eyelids as wide open as they would possibly go, to see the Dodger plunge
his hand into the old gentleman’s pocket, and draw from thence a handkerchief!
To see him hand the same to Charley Bates; and finally to behold them, both
running away round the corner at full speed!
assignments.summary: Oliver witnesses the Dodger steal a handkerchief from the old gentleman's pocket and hand it to Charley Bates before both boys flee.
assignments.best_quote: What was Oliver's horror and alarm as he stood a few paces off, looking on with his eyelids as wide open as they would possibly go, to see the Dodger plunge his hand into the old gentleman's pocket, and draw from thence a handkerchief!

assignments.text:
In an instant the whole mystery of the hankerchiefs, and the watches, and the
jewels, and the Jew, rushed upon the boy’s mind.
assignments.summary: Oliver realizes that all the stolen goods in Fagin's house—handkerchiefs, watches, jewels—are the proceeds of picking pockets.
assignments.best_quote: In an instant the whole mystery of the hankerchiefs, and the watches, and the jewels, and the Jew, rushed upon the boy's mind.

assignments.text:
“Stop thief! Stop thief!” There is a passion  for hunting something 
deeply implanted in the human breast. One wretched breathless child, panting
with exhaustion; terror in his looks; agony in his eyes; large drops of
perspiration streaming down his face; strains every nerve to make head upon his
pursuers; and as they follow on his track, and gain upon him every instant,
they hail his decreasing strength with joy. “Stop thief!” Ay, stop him for
God’s sake, were it only in mercy!
assignments.summary: Oliver's exhausted, terrified flight contrasts sharply with the crowd's sadistic pleasure in his suffering; Dickens appeals for mercy.
assignments.best_quote: One wretched breathless child, panting with exhaustion; terror in his looks; agony in his eyes; large drops of perspiration streaming down his face; strains every nerve to make head upon his pursuers; and as they follow on his track, and gain upon him every instant, they hail his decreasing strength with joy. "Stop thief!" Ay, stop him for God's sake, were it only in mercy!

assignments.text:
“He has been hurt already,” said the old gentleman in conclusion. “And I fear,”
he added, with great energy, looking towards the bar, “I really fear that he is
ill.”
assignments.summary: Mr. Brownlow expresses fear for Oliver's physical well-being, noting he has been hurt and appears gravely ill.
assignments.best_quote: And I fear, he added, with great energy, looking towards the bar, I really fear that he is ill.

assignments.text:
Oliver tried to reply but his tongue failed him. He was deadly pale; and the
whole place seemed turning round and round.
assignments.summary: Oliver cannot speak, becomes pale, and feels the courtroom spinning around him.
assignments.best_quote: Oliver tried to reply but his tongue failed him. He was deadly pale; and the whole place seemed turning round and round.
